company_name: Postal Savings Bank of China Co., Ltd. (PSBC)
model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on CET1 retention, net debt zero (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Perpetual bonds (other equity instruments) at par, senior to ordinary
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 interim balance sheet, RMB150,000m; FY2025 AR line 2950 RMB149,996m. Flows are before the RMB7.2bn/yr distributions to these holders, so par is deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (4.4%) cross-checked to ordinary BVPS 3yr CAGR (4.3%); equity CAGR rejected as inflated by the RMB130bn FY2025 placement
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Ordinary equity 3yr CAGR 13.9% vs revenue 2.0% and EPS -5.0%: divergence is the Jun-2025 MOF placement (shares 99,161m -> 120,095m, +21%) and perpetual-bond issuance, not organic compounding. Per-share book grew 4.3%/yr; EPS fell on the dilution (FY2025 EPS 0.73 vs 0.81).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs not meaningful for a bank (OCF swings with deposit/interbank flows). Revenue (operating income) grew 1.9% in FY2025 and 7.2% in H1-2026; net profit grew 1.1% in FY2025 and 4.6% in H1-2026; ROE fell from 11.9% (FY2021/22) to 8.67% (FY2025) and ROAA from 0.64% to 0.49%.

scenario_narratives.base: PSBC keeps growing its balance sheet at high-single digits for two more years (RWA +12% in 2026, +8% in 2027) under the 'five priorities' policy mandate, while NIM drifts from 1.63% toward ~1.5% and revenue grows ~4% on volume and fees. The Q1-2026 agency-fee cut and cost-to-income gains hold the PBT margin near 26%. Capital retained to hold CET1 at 10.0% absorbs most of the profit until RWA growth decelerates to 3.5% in the 2030s; the ~RMB32bn dividend is therefore partly funded by letting the MOF buffer drift, exactly as H1-2026 showed (10.53% -> 10.04%). Ordinary holders rank behind RMB150bn of perpetuals. The result is an ROE of ~7-8% against a 9.5% cost of equity: the bank is worth less than book.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM stabilises in 2027 as deposit repricing catches up, fee income keeps compounding double digits, and the agency-fee renegotiation with China Post sticks, lifting the PBT margin to 28.5%. Management lets CET1 settle at 9.75% and RWA growth converges to revenue growth sooner, so payout capacity recovers to ~60% of profit and the dividend becomes earnings-covered. Terminal multiple capped at 16x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bear: PBOC easing continues and NIM reaches 1.3-1.4%; with coverage already halved, a property/SME/policy-loan NPL cycle must be provisioned from P&L and the agency-fee rate reverts, taking the PBT margin to 23%. Policy-directed RWA growth continues at 11%/8%/7% while the regulator insists the 10.25% CET1 buffer is held, so retention exceeds profit in 2027-28: FCFE turns negative and the gap is met by another dilutive placement or a dividend cut. After the RMB150bn perpetual claim, ordinary equity is worth little -- this scenario sits at or below the zero floor and says so.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A deposit-rich, state-backed retail bank earning ~7-8% on ordinary equity against a 9.5% CNY cost of equity, with balance-sheet growth that consumes more capital than it generates. Value = PV of FCFE (profit less CET1 retention) at the cost of equity, less perpetual bonds at par, converted CNY -> HKD. At 0.54x H1-2026 book (RMB8.71/share) the H-share already prices ROE below CoE; what it does not price is that the ~4.6% dividend yield is being paid out of capital rather than free cash flow while RWA grows 8-12%. The required-return table shows what rate the market is applying -- roughly a 7% dividend-yield lens -- against the house 9.5%.
key_risks_to_valuation: RWA growth path: every 1pp of sustained RWA growth at a 10% CET1 target costs ~RMB10bn/yr of FCFE (~RMB1.2/share of value over the horizon); the single swing variable, as on 0998.HK
CET1 target: holding 10.25% instead of 9.75% is ~RMB50bn of retained capital over the horizon
NIM: each 10bp on RMB17tn of interest-earning assets is ~RMB17bn of revenue (~4.5% of operating income)
Deposit agency fee (~RMB112bn/yr, ~30% of operating income): renegotiated downward in Q1-2026; a reversal or a politically-set rate swings the PBT margin by several points either way
Perpetual bonds deducted at par (RMB150bn, RMB1.25/share CNY): capitalising their ~RMB7bn coupons at the cost of equity instead would add ~RMB0.8/share
Cost of equity: the price implies ~7% on the dividend; each 1pp on the 9.5% rate moves the base IV by roughly 15-20%
A/H premium of ~17%: the H-share can re-rate on southbound flows independent of fundamentals

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 1658.HK at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 4.48-5.78 HKD. A-share 601658.SS from the same API for the A/H note.
data_sources.fx: Yahoo HKDCNY=X at 2026-10-16T14:30Z, inverted to CNY -> HKD.
data_sources.financials: 1658.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics export: FY2018-FY2025 annual, quarterlies and half-years to H1-2026, bank KPIs); H1-2026 interim report for RWA, net CET1 capital, perpetual bonds, allowance coverage, deposit agency fee; FY2025 annual report for RWA history, perpetual-bond distributions (line 17053), tax paid, dividends.

inputs.share_count_basis: 120,095m ordinary shares (A + H, one class) at 30 Jun 2026 per H1-2026 interim; post the Jun-2025 RMB130bn MOF-anchored A-share placement of 20,934m shares. No convertibles or options; perpetual bonds are non-convertible and are deducted at par in equity_bridge. Held flat: SBC is nil and no further non-SBC issuance is assumed in base/bull; the bear path's capital shortfall is shown as negative FCFE rather than as a modelled dilutive raise.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank: deposits (RMB16.5tn), debt securities issued (RMB251bn incl. tier-2) and central-bank borrowings are operating funding, not net debt; cash and central-bank balances (RMB1.40tn) are operating liquidity. All set to zero and the FCFE flow is discounted at the cost of equity, per SKILL.md's bank row.
inputs.fcfe_fy2025_note: last_fcf is FY2025 FCFE = net profit attributable to Bank shareholders RMB87,404m less CET1 retention required by FY2025 RWA growth (RWA 8,617,743 -> 9,533,914, x 10.0% target = RMB91,617m) = -RMB4,213m. FY2025 dividends (RMB26.2bn) were therefore funded by the RMB130bn placement, not by earnings. OCF (RMB424bn) is meaningless for a bank and is not used. reported_fcf is set equal so the owner-FCF identity holds with sbc = interest_income = 0.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme disclosed in FY2025 annual report or H1-2026 interim (state-controlled bank; SBC-zero market). Kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in RMB (CNY) millions; H-share quoted in HKD on HKEX. fx_rate is CNY -> HKD = 1/0.8519 = 1.1739 (Yahoo HKDCNY=X 0.8519 at 2026-10-16T14:30Z). Dual listing: A-share 601658.SS closed RMB5.51 on 2026-10-16 vs H-share HKD5.515 = RMB4.70, an A/H premium of ~17% -- normal for Chinese state banks, so the A-share is NOT a parity check of the rate; the rate itself is checked against the Yahoo CNYHKD cross. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD to match current_price.
inputs.capital_anchor: 30 Jun 2026: net CET1 capital RMB1,038,704m on RWA RMB10,346,860m = 10.04% (Dec-25: 1,003,478 / 9,533,914 = 10.53%; Dec-24: 824,191 / 8,617,743 = 9.56%). Regulatory CET1 minimum incl. buffers 8.00% (H1-2026 note). RWA grew 8.5% in six months; CET1 ratio drifted down 0.49pp despite retained H1 profit.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.5% in CNY, applied to all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows). Built as China 10y CGB ~1.8% + ~6.5% China ERP x beta ~1.0 = ~8.3%, plus ~1.2pp for state-directed capital allocation and the related-party agency-fee dependency that ordinary H-share holders cannot influence. Matches the folder's 9.5% for CCB/0939.HK (Big Four), one point below CITIC/0998.HK's 10.5% joint-stock premium: PSBC is Big Six, retail-deposit funded, MOF-recapitalised, AAA domestic / A1-A international. Not a USD rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial (lease liabilities RMB10.9bn vs RMB19.8tn assets) and already inside operating expenses via depreciation of right-of-use assets; no adjustment, no lease line, no lease debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is RMB219m of RMB87,623m profit (0.25%). Folded into the cash_tax_rate_path (10.5% = ~10.25% effective tax + 0.25% NCI leakage) so modelled year-1 NOPAT ties to attributable profit; no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.perpetual_bond_treatment: RMB150,000m of undated capital bonds (other equity instruments, H1-2026; Jun-2026 RMB30bn issue replaced the Q1 redemption) rank ahead of ordinary shares. Profit attributable to their holders was RMB7,161m in FY2025 (RMB6,342m FY2024). Charged once: the flows use net profit attributable to Bank shareholders BEFORE those distributions, and the instruments are deducted at par in equity_bridge (coupons reset at market, instruments are rolled at par; discounting a senior fixed claim at the equity rate would understate it).
inputs.engine_mapping: Engine fields are relabelled for a bank: revenue = operating income (NII + net fees + other non-interest income); ebitda_margin = profit-before-tax margin after operating expenses (incl. the China Post deposit agency fee), taxes and surcharges, and credit impairment; sbc, lease, D&A and working capital = 0; cash_tax_rate = effective tax (~10%, structurally low from tax-exempt government-bond income) + NCI leakage; capex_pct = CET1 capital retained to hold the target CET1 ratio on the projected RWA path (RWA_t x target - CET1_{t-1}), from Dec-25 CET1 RMB1,003,478m and RWA RMB9,533,914m. FCFE = PBT x (1 - tax) - CET1 retention, discounted at the cost of equity; equity value less perpetual bonds at par, divided by 120,095m shares, converted CNY -> HKD.
inputs.notes: Model: bank FCFE at cost of equity (residual-income-equivalent) through the Drivers engine with net debt zero, per SKILL.md's bank row and the folder's 0998.HK / 0939.HK precedent; an owner-FCF DCF on OCF would be meaningless (deposits are not debt). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Deposit agency fee to China Post Group: the H1-2026 'deposit agency fee and others' line is RMB55,964m for six months (~RMB112bn/yr, ~30% of operating income), far larger than the RMB24-25bn cited in the handoff; it is the single largest opex item and its Q1-2026 proactive rate cut is what drove the cost-to-income ratio down 4.17pp. Price is the HKEX regular close of 16 Oct 2026 (52-week range 4.48-5.78), not after-hours. Balance-sheet and share-count anchors are 30 Jun 2026 (latest filing); revenue base and RWA/CET1 retention start are FY2025 (Dec-25), the last full year, with H1-2026 informing year-1 growth and the CET1 target.

bear.growth_rates_note: Further LPR cuts take NIM to ~1.3-1.4%; NII falls in absolute terms in 2027-28 and fee growth only partly offsets.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: PBT margin to 23%: allowance coverage has already been drawn from 419% to 215%, so an NPL cycle (property, SME, policy-directed lending) must be provisioned from P&L; the agency-fee agreement reverts at the next review.
bear.capex_pct_note: CET1 target 10.25% (regulator wants the MOF buffer held) on RWA growth [11, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4.5, 4, 4, 4, 4]% as state-directed lending continues regardless of returns. Retention exceeds post-tax profit in FY2027-28, so FCFE is negative -- the gap would be met by another placement or a dividend cut.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5%/2.5% = 14.64x binds under the 15x cap.

base.growth_rates_note: Operating income: FY2026 +5.5% (H1-2026 ran +7.2% on fee +12% and other non-interest +12%, haircut for H2 NIM pressure), then 4% as loan volume outruns NIM compression (1.63% H1-2026 drifting to ~1.5%), fading to 3% nominal-GDP-like growth.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Profit-before-tax margin 26.3% FY2026 (H1-2026 29.9% vs H1-2025 32.3%: H1 is seasonally ~3-4pp above FY, and PBT fell 0.9% YoY as impairment rose), vs 27.6% FY2025 / 27.1% FY2024. Steady 26.0% thereafter: agency-fee cut and cost-to-income gains offset NIM erosion and coverage normalising from 215% toward 180-200%.
base.capex_pct_note: CET1 retention at a 10.0% target ratio on RWA growth [12, 8, 7, 6, 5.5, 5, 4.5, 4, 3.5, 3.5]% (H1-2026 RWA +8.5% in six months; FY2025 +10.6%); the 10.53% Dec-25 ratio drifts to 10.0% in year 1 (observed 10.04% at Jun-26) and is held there. Retained capital peaks at RMB85bn in FY2027 against ~RMB92bn of post-tax profit, so FCFE is a fraction of the ~RMB32bn dividend until RWA growth decelerates.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: FY2025 effective tax 10.8%, FY2024 8.3%, FY2023 5.6%, H1-2026 10.1% -- structurally low from tax-exempt CGB and local-government bond income; 10.5% includes the 0.25% NCI slice.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5%/3.0% = 15.85x FCFE binds under the 16x cap. Terminal retention of 11.1% of revenue (RWA +3.5%) leaves a ~53% payout of terminal-year profit, consistent with ROE of ~7% and 3% growth.

bull.growth_rates_note: H1-2026's +7.2% holds for the year; NIM stabilises at ~1.6% in 2027 as deposit repricing catches up; fee 'second growth curve' keeps compounding double digits.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: PBT margin ramps to 28.5%: the Q1-2026 agency-fee rate cut sticks and compounds, cost-to-income keeps falling, impairment stays at the FY2025 run-rate.
bull.capex_pct_note: CET1 target 9.75% (management lets the MOF buffer drift back toward the pre-raise 9.5-10% range) on RWA growth [11, 7, 6, 5, 4.5, 4, 4, 3.5, 3.5, 3.5]% -- balance-sheet growth converges to revenue growth sooner.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: the FY2025 dividend was not earnings-covered (FCFE negative, funded by the placement), CET1 has already given back half the MOF uplift in six months, NIM has fallen every year since 2018, coverage has halved, and capital allocation is state-directed with a related-party agency fee that is ~30% of operating income. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things at once -- NIM stabilisation, the agency-fee cut sticking, and RWA growth decelerating to revenue growth.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
